adequacy_checks.all_must_pass: If any check fails, the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE. INCONCLUSIVE is terminal for this protocol version; it is not retried by silent adjustment. A revised protocol is a new frozen record with the reason stated.

competing_modes.criterion: The selected f1 peak must exceed the highest competing peak in the search band by a factor >= 10 in AMPLITUDE (magnitude, not power). Competing-peak search excludes the selected peak's own main lobe, defined as +-2 raw (unpadded) bins around the selected peak bin.
competing_modes.rationale: Rules out contamination by higher bending modes, torsional modes, or numerical artifacts. Amplitude ratio is the directly observed quantity.

frequency_resolution.criterion: Raw (unpadded) FFT bin width df = 1/T_window <= 0.5 Hz, computed from the ACTUAL sampled interval (last timestamp minus first timestamp of the measurement window as read from output), not the nominal deck duration. The actual T_window must be >= 2.0 s for the full window.
frequency_resolution.rationale: Strict bound on spectral spacing. Interpolated accuracy is validated separately (see estimator.validation) and is not a substitute for this bound.

sampling_uniformity.criterion: All inter-sample intervals in the measurement window must satisfy |dt - 0.0005| < 1e-6 s; no missing samples (window sample count must equal round(T_window / 0.0005) + 1 within +-1).
sampling_uniformity.rationale: Non-uniform sampling invalidates the FFT bin-width arithmetic and the interpolation validation, which assumed uniform cadence.

signal_strength.aggregation: RMS of the FFT magnitude spectrum over the quiet band.
signal_strength.criterion: (a) Peak ringdown amplitude (max |tip DZ| over the first 5 cycles after t_settle) >= 100x the quiet-band RMS, where 100x is an AMPLITUDE ratio. (b) Block-RMS decay: split the measurement window into 10 equal blocks; RMS of block 10 >= 1% of RMS of block 1. Block RMS (not instantaneous displacement, which crosses zero).
signal_strength.quiet_band_note: Above the search band and clear of f2 (~255 Hz) and f3 (~715 Hz); below Nyquist (1000 Hz) with margin.
signal_strength.rationale: Adequate SNR throughout; guards against interpreting a decayed-to-noise tail.
signal_strength.zero_noise_estimate: If the quiet-band RMS is exactly zero (or below 1e-300, the log floor), the SNR is unverifiable -> INCONCLUSIVE. A zero noise estimate is not evidence of infinite SNR.

stability_across_windows.criterion: Independent f1 estimates from the first half-window [0.6, 1.6] and second half-window [1.6, 2.6] must agree within 0.5% relative. Exact boundaries as stated; halves are contiguous and non-overlapping.
stability_across_windows.rationale: A stationary modal frequency must be window-independent.

interpolation.convention: Symmetric Hann (NumPy: 0.5 - 0.5*cos(2*pi*k/(n-1))), applied after mean removal.
interpolation.padding_note: Zero-padding factor applied to the windowed segment length; FFT length = 8 * n_samples.
interpolation.quantity: log10 of the FFT magnitude spectrum. Frozen on validation evidence (lowest max error among the three tested quantities).
interpolation.refinement: Parabolic interpolation on the log10-magnitude using the peak bin and its two immediate neighbors; fractional-bin offset clipped to [-1, 1]; added to the peak bin frequency.

estimator.name: Hann-windowed FFT peak estimator with log-magnitude parabolic refinement

peak_selection.band_note: [0.7, 1.3] x f_ref. f2 ~ 255 Hz well outside.
peak_selection.rule: Highest log10-magnitude peak in the search band. Record the interpolated frequency, the raw peak bin, the fractional offset, and the prominence (amplitude ratio to the highest competing peak outside the main lobe).
peak_selection.tie_or_ambiguity: If two peaks in the band are within a factor of 2 in amplitude, the competing-modes adequacy check governs (likely INCONCLUSIVE). No analyst discretion to prefer the peak nearer the reference.

exact_window_boundaries.note: Boundaries refer to output timestamps. The first/last samples used are the ones nearest to (within 0.25 ms of) these boundaries; the actual timestamps are recorded.

steps: Extract face-averaged tip DZ over the measurement window at the /TFILE cadence.
Verify sampling uniformity (adequacy check) BEFORE spectral analysis.
Compute the FFT magnitude spectrum; take log10.
Peak-pick and parabolically refine per the interpolation spec.
preprocessing.t_settle_note: Measurement starts at 0.6 s, ~0.1 s after release completion (0.501 s); the release transient is excluded by the window start, not by a separate t_settle parameter.

validation.conclusion: The claimed accuracy (~0.05 Hz) is validated with ~25x margin for this exact estimator configuration. Log-magnitude frozen on evidence.
validation.max_error_note: Worst case: half-window, strong decay (tau=0.5 s), noise at the permitted level, competing mode at the permitted 10% amplitude. All 480 cases per quantity bounded by ~0.002 Hz.
validation.sweep: fractional-bin offsets {0.0,0.1,0.25,0.4,0.5} x phases {0,pi/4,pi/2,pi} x decay {none, tau=2.0 s, tau=0.5 s} x (noise, competing-mode) {(0,0),(0.005,0),(0,0.1),(0.005,0.1)} x {full 2.0 s window, half 1.0 s window}

fext_availability.conclusion: Direct applied-load output is NOT available in OpenCourant 33e68517. Corroboration proceeds via the impulse/momentum balance below.
evidence: No 'FEXT' nodal /TH variable keyword in starter (hm_read_thgrou.F) or engine (thnod.F).
'TFEXT' exists but is a /TH/SECT (cross-section) variable only.
'PEXT' is nodal pressure (NODA_PEXT / NODA_SURF), not a force witness.
'WFEXT' is global external work (energy), a cumulative quantity.

excitation.method: Step-unload from the quasi-static 1000 N state. Load ramps 0 -> 1000 N over [0, 0.1] s (same /FUNCT/1 as the static verification), holds to t_release_start, then ramps to zero over [t_release_start, t_release_complete].

release_completion_check.criterion_A_prerelease: J_applied over window A = [0.498, 0.500] s must satisfy |J_applied - (-2.0)| <= 0.1 N.s (applied load -1000 N over 2 ms).
release_completion_check.criterion_B_postrelease: J_applied over window B = [0.502, 0.504] s must satisfy |J_applied| <= 0.1 N.s (load at zero; bound detects a stuck or partially released load, not a precise zero).
release_completion_check.definitions: Pz(t) = global Z-momentum (/TH 'Z-MOMENTUM'), positive +Z. J_wall(t) = summed wall REACZ cumulative impulse, positive +Z. J_applied[ta,tb] = [Pz(tb)-Pz(ta)] - [J_wall(tb)-J_wall(ta)]. Uses output samples within each window; each window must contain >= 3 samples; endpoint samples must lie within 0.25 ms of the stated boundary or the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE.
release_completion_check.verdict: If both criteria pass, the release completed between 0.500 and 0.502 s, consistent with the deck-specified 0.501 s. If either fails, the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE (excitation did not occur as specified). This check is against the 0.501 s release COMPLETION, not the 0.500 s release start.
release_completion_check.windows_note: Windows are 2 ms (4 output samples at 0.5 ms cadence): short enough to locate the 1 ms release, long enough for a stable momentum difference.

excitation.t_release_ramp_note: 1 ms ramp: fast enough to approximate a step release, non-instantaneous to avoid exciting non-physical ultra-high-frequency content.

formulation.note: Identical to the verified static formulation; the dynamic gate tests the mass/stiffness distribution, not a new formulation.

mesh: fine (40x8x8, 2560 bricks) — the verified mesh from the static campaign.

outcome_definitions.FAIL: All adequacy checks pass, release completion verified, and |f_est - f_ref| / f_ref > 0.02.
outcome_definitions.INCONCLUSIVE: Any adequacy check fails; or the release completion check fails; or sampling is non-uniform. Terminal for this protocol version.
outcome_definitions.PASS: All adequacy checks pass, release completion verified, and |f_est - f_ref| / f_ref <= 0.02.

assumptions: Uniform cross-section, linear elastic, small deflections.
Ideal clamped boundary (all DOFs fixed at wall).
No damping in the analytical model.
Material: E = 200 GPa, rho = 7850 kg/m^3; geometry L = 1.0 m, 0.05 x 0.05 m section.
reference.shear_correction_note: Timoshenko shear correction is 0.195% of bending deflection at L/h = 20; Euler-Bernoulli is an adequate reference.
reference.systematic_offset_note: The 3D solid model includes shear flexibility and 3D clamp effects absent from the EB idealization; a small systematic offset is accommodated by the tolerance, not corrected for.

response_check.criterion: Mean face-averaged tip DZ over [0.3, 0.5] s must be within 5% of the static fine-mesh value (-3.254806 mm); the post-release signal (t > 0.6 s) must exhibit zero crossings (oscillation about zero).
response_check.note: SEPARATE from the release verification. This checks the structural response behaved as expected; it does not establish when excitation ended.
response_check.purpose: Sanity check that the model reached the quasi-static state before release and rang down afterward.

revision_of: dynamic-protocol-2026-10-08 (commit 22b48ed1), preserved as the reviewed version. v1 is not ready to run; this v2 addresses the review findings explicitly.
revision_summary: Raw 0.5 Hz bin bound kept strict: t_end extended to 2.7 s giving >= 2.0 s usable measurement ([0.6, 2.6]); actual sampled interval checked, not nominal duration.
Interpolation frozen on validation evidence: log10-magnitude parabola, symmetric Hann, 8x padding; synthetic sweep (1440 cases) bounds error at 0.00184 Hz.

Release verified against 0.501 s completion via impulse/momentum balance (direct FEXT unavailable in this OpenCourant version; source-confirmed); displacement retained as a separate response check only.

Adequacy thresholds made executable: amplitude (not power) ratios; quiet band [400,600] Hz with RMS aggregation and zero-estimate rule; block-RMS decay; main-lobe exclusion; sampling uniformity; exact window boundaries.

sampling.note: 2 kHz sampling gives ~49 points per f1 cycle. Measurement window [0.6, 2.6] s = 2.0 s nominal, ~78 cycles at f1; actual interval verified from output timestamps.

status: FROZEN v2 — pending review. No run launched under this protocol.

tolerance.heuristic_note: 'Frequency error ~ half the static-deflection error' remains a HEURISTIC rationale for choosing 2%, not an established bound for this mesh. No dynamic convergence evidence exists yet; the tolerance is a proposed engineering criterion.
tolerance.rationale: Consistent with the static gate (±2% on fine-mesh deflection). Tight enough to discriminate a wrong mass or stiffness distribution; loose enough not to punish the EB-vs-3D idealization gap.
